metaDescription: Six USB rechargeable kitchen scales compared by capacity, charging port, battery life and platform material, so you can stop replacing coin cells and AAAs.
introParagraphs: A rechargeable kitchen scale swaps disposable batteries for a built-in cell you top up with a USB cable. The appeal is simple: no dead coin cell halfway through a recipe and no drawer of spare batteries. Most of the models here charge over Type-C, and a few offer a battery backup.

The six picks cover capacities from 22 lb to 33 lb, with 1 g steps on nearly all of them. They differ in platform material, whether they are sealed against water, and how long the battery is said to last. We evaluated them from product specs, listing details and buyer feedback, not hands-on testing.
Before you buy, check the charging port, the stated battery life and whether the scale still works while plugged in. Those three details decide how often you will think about power.

products.name: Etekcity 22lb Rechargeable Kitchen Scale, IPX6

specList.label: Units

products.description:
This Etekcity scale weighs from 2 g up to 22 lb in 1 g increments and charges through a USB-C port with a cable in the box. The battery is listed at 300mAh, which is small but sufficient for a device that sleeps most of the day. An IPX6 waterproof design lets you wipe it down or measure liquids without worrying about splashes.

Five units are on offer: ounces, pounds and ounces, grams, milliliters for milk and water, and fluid ounces for the same two liquids. That range makes it useful for both baking and coffee-adjacent jobs. The 22 lb ceiling is generous for a compact scale.

The listing gives a battery size but no hours of life, so you cannot plan around a number. It tops out below the 33 lb models, which matters only if you weigh heavy items. Compared with the Ultrean IPX7 33lb Rechargeable Food Scale, it has a lower water rating and a smaller cell, while the CROWNFUL 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale gives you an AAA backup that the Etekcity lacks.

products.name: Ultrean IPX7 33lb Rechargeable Food Scale
products.description:
The Ultrean scale carries a 700mAh lithium battery, the largest cell listed in this group. The listing says it can last up to 4 months, based on light daily use, and it charges over Type-C. Capacity reaches 33 lb with 1 g or 0.1 oz steps and a 2 g minimum.

It is also sealed to an IPX7 rating and described as sink-safe, so you can rinse it under running water. That is useful after weighing sticky honey or raw meat. The combination of long battery life and washability makes it the most low-maintenance pick here.

The tradeoff is that sealed designs usually have a simple platform without many frills. You should still keep the charging port dry and closed after washing. Compared with the Etekcity 22lb Rechargeable Kitchen Scale, IPX6, you gain a bigger cell and a stronger water rating, and against the izeyu 33lb USB Rechargeable Kitchen Scale you get a stated four-month figure rather than a standby count.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want the longest stated battery life and a scale that can be rinsed in the sink.

products.name: CROWNFUL 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale
products.description:
The CROWNFUL runs on a Type-C charging connector or two AAA batteries, and both the USB cable and batteries are included. That dual power is its main selling point. If the built-in pack runs low in the middle of a bake, you can drop in AAAs instead of hunting for a charger.

The platform is a large 304 stainless steel panel meant to hold bigger containers. Measuring runs from 3 g to 33 lb or 15 kg with 1 g steps. A larger panel helps when you weigh in a stockpot or a mixing bowl.

The 3 g minimum is a little higher than the 2 g floors on the Etekcity and Ultrean, so very small additions are less precise. There is no water rating listed in the brief, so keep spills off it. Compared with the Diyife 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale, the CROWNFUL highlights its 304 steel and the AAA fallback.
products.bestFor: Cooks who like a safety net of AAA batteries and a big steel platform for large containers.

Measures from 3 g all the way up to 33 lb
cons: Higher 3 g minimum than some rivals
No water rating given in the brief

products.name: Diyife 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale
products.description:
The Diyife is a 304 stainless steel scale that uses four high-precision sensors to read up to 33 lb. The platform measures 7.5 by 5.5 inches and is only 0.5 inches thick. A backlit LCD with white lettering shows the weight in a 2.2 by 0.9 inch window.

Two power options are offered: standard batteries or a USB rechargeable pack with the cable included. You turn it on with a single button. The thin profile slides into a drawer, and the metal top is easy to wipe.

The display window is smaller than on some rivals, and the brief lists no water rating or battery hours. That means you should treat it as a basic daily scale. Compared with the CROWNFUL 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale, its platform is smaller, and compared with the GGQ 33lb Rechargeable Digital Kitchen Scale it has no glass panel or touch controls.
products.bestFor: Cooks with limited drawer space who want a thin steel scale with a backlit display.

Battery or USB charging both available

Small display window of 2.2 by 0.9 inches

products.name: GGQ 33lb Rechargeable Digital Kitchen Scale
products.description:
The GGQ scale has a waterproof, anti-collision glass weighing panel over four high-precision load sensors. Screen touch controls and a large LCD make it feel more modern than the button-based models. It covers five units: grams, kilograms, pounds and ounces, ounces and milliliters.

The tare button subtracts the weight of a mug, plate or bowl so you can add food without doing math. Glass is smooth and wipes clean, and it suits a kitchen with a sleek counter. It is rechargeable, though the brief does not list the port type or battery life.

Glass can chip if you drop a pan on it, and touch controls can be fussy with wet fingers. Compared with the Etekcity 22lb Rechargeable Kitchen Scale, IPX6, it lacks a stated IP rating and a USB-C cable detail. Against the Diyife, it offers a glass top rather than steel.

products.name: izeyu 33lb USB Rechargeable Kitchen Scale
products.description:
The izeyu scale measures up to 15 kg or 33 lb in 1 g or 0.1 oz steps and offers six measuring ranges. A stainless steel top is described, along with automatic and manual shutoff. Its battery recharges over USB.

The headline number is over 120 days of standby, which suggests you can charge it only a few times a year if it mostly sits idle. That is a standby figure, not a count of weighing sessions. Weighing for long stretches will drain it faster.

Six units help with international recipes. The listing does not state a water rating, so avoid soaking it. Next to the Ultrean IPX7 33lb Rechargeable Food Scale, the izeyu gives a standby figure while the Ultrean gives a figure tied to daily use, and next to the CROWNFUL it has no AAA backup.
products.bestFor: Occasional bakers who want a large-capacity scale that holds charge for months in a drawer.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A rechargeable scale is only convenient if you already own the right cable. Type-C is the common standard now and is easy to replace. The Etekcity 22lb Rechargeable Kitchen Scale, IPX6, Ultrean IPX7 33lb Rechargeable Food Scale and CROWNFUL 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale all list Type-C. Check that the cable is included, since a few listings leave it out.

Battery numbers vary in meaning, so read them closely. Hours of use, days of standby and months of light daily use are different promises. The Ultrean claims up to 4 months with a 700mAh cell, while the izeyu lists over 120 days of standby. The Etekcity lists 300mAh but no hours.

A scale that dies while the dough is half-measured is annoying. Models that accept AAA batteries or work while plugged in remove that risk. The CROWNFUL accepts two AAA batteries as an alternative, and the Diyife lists both battery and USB power. Pure rechargeable units like the izeyu need charging ahead of time.

Kitchen scales meet flour, oil and spills. IPX6 handles strong splashes, while IPX7 is rated for brief immersion. The Ultrean is IPX7 and described as sink-safe, and the Etekcity is IPX6. Keep the charging port closed and dry on any sealed model.

Capacity should exceed your heaviest load by a comfortable margin. Most baking never nears 22 lb, but stockpots and big batches can. Four of these picks reach 33 lb, and the Etekcity stops at 22 lb. The CROWNFUL has a large panel, while the Diyife platform is 7.5 by 5.5 inches.

Stainless steel resists stains, and glass wipes clean but can chip. Touch controls look sleek but can misbehave with wet fingers. The GGQ 33lb Rechargeable Digital Kitchen Scale uses glass and touch controls, and the Diyife and izeyu use steel. Pick the surface that suits your counter habits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and charging
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at port type, battery size and any stated life figure. The Ultrean leads with a 700mAh cell and up to 4 months, and the CROWNFUL adds AAA backup. Listings that gave no battery life lost points for planning ability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and precision
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared maximum load and increments. Four picks reach 33 lb, the Etekcity reaches 22 lb, and all list 1 g steps. Minimum weights of 2 g on the Etekcity and Ultrean and 3 g on the CROWNFUL were treated as a real difference.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water resistance
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for sealing claims. The Ultrean at IPX7 is the strongest and the Etekcity at IPX6 is next. Others list no rating, so they were treated as splash-careful only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and display
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the weighing surface and how readable the screen is. CROWNFUL's 304 steel panel is large, Diyife is thin with a backlit display, and GGQ uses glass with touch controls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted units, shutoff features and backup power. The izeyu offers six units with automatic and manual shutoff, and the Etekcity offers five units with milk and water modes. These extras were a tiebreaker rather than a headline. A scale with fewer features but a clearer battery story outranked a crowded one with vague power details.

howToChoose.intro: Two power philosophies cover different risks.

cards.label: Dual power
cards.text: Battery plus USB gives you a fallback when the pack is flat. CROWNFUL 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale and Diyife 33lb Rechargeable Stainless Kitchen Scale offer this. Pick one if you cook at odd hours and cannot wait for a charge.

faq.q: Is a rechargeable scale better than a battery scale?
faq.a: It is more convenient if you weigh often, since you skip replacing cells. A built-in pack can degrade over years, though, so a model with AAA backup like the CROWNFUL offers insurance. Choose based on how reliably you remember to charge.

faq.q: How do I choose between Type-C and standard USB?
faq.a: Type-C is easier to plug in and widely shared with phones and tablets. The Etekcity, Ultrean and CROWNFUL list Type-C explicitly. For others, check the listing before assuming a cable standard.

faq.q: Can I use the scale while it charges?
faq.a: The brief does not say for most models, so do not assume it. If cooking while plugged in matters, look for a dual power design such as the Diyife or CROWNFUL. Otherwise charge between uses.

faq.q: Does IPX7 mean I can wash it in the dishwasher?
faq.a: No. IPX7 refers to brief immersion in water, not heat, detergent or pressure jets. The Ultrean is described as sink-safe, so rinse it by hand and dry the port.

A scale below its minimum may read unreliably or show nothing. The Etekcity and Ultrean list 2 g, and the CROWNFUL lists 3 g. If you weigh small spice amounts, choose a lower minimum or use a dedicated precision scale.

faq.q: How long will the battery last overall?
faq.a: Listings give different kinds of figures. Ultrean lists up to 4 months of light daily use, and izeyu lists over 120 days of standby. Neither is a guarantee, and the pack will fade over years like any lithium cell.

For most home cooking it is more than you need, but it is useful for stockpots and bulk food. The Etekcity at 22 lb is plenty for typical baking. Larger capacity does not reduce accuracy at small amounts on these listings, but check the minimum weight. Also consider storage, because a scale that reaches 33 lb often has a larger platform that takes more drawer or cabinet room, as the CROWNFUL panel does.

faq.q: Should I leave a rechargeable scale plugged in all the time?
faq.a: Not unless the listing says it is designed for it. Most small lithium packs are happiest charged when low and then unplugged. Set a reminder when the display shows a low battery indicator, such as the LO message that some models use, and top it up then.
